source.author: verg
source.text: Nec minus et miseri diversa in parte Latini innumeras struxere pyras, et corpora partim multa virum terrae infodiunt avectaque partim finitimos tollunt in agros urbique remittunt, cetera confusaeque ingentem caedis acervum nec numero nec honore cremant: tunc undique vasti certatim crebris collucent ignibus agri.
source.text_original: Nec minus et miseri diversa in parte Latini / innumeras struxere pyras, et corpora partim / multa virum terrae infodiunt avectaque partim / finitimos tollunt in agros urbique remittunt, / cetera confusaeque ingentem caedis acervum / nec numero nec honore cremant: tunc undique vasti / certatim crebris collucent ignibus agri.
source.text_english: Not less did the wretched Latins, in a different part, build countless pyres, and some of the bodies of the men they buried in the earth, while others they carried away and bore to neighboring fields and sent back to the city; the rest they burned, along with a vast heap of slaughter, in confused fashion, with neither count nor honor: then on every side the wide fields shone in rivalry with frequent fires.

reuse.author: val
reuse.text: proximus hinc Butes Actaeis dives ab oris; innumeras nam claudit apes longaque superbus fuscat nube diem, dum plenas nectare cellas pandit et in dulcem reges dimittit Hymetton.
reuse.text_original: proximus hinc Butes Actaeis dives ab oris; / innumeras nam claudit apes longaque superbus / fuscat nube diem, dum plenas nectare cellas / pandit et in dulcem reges dimittit Hymetton.
reuse.text_english: Next from here was Butes, rich from the Actaean shores; for he keeps innumerable bees shut up and, proud, darkens the day with a long cloud, as he opens the cells full of nectar and sends the kings out into sweet Hymettus.
